subject: Proposal: phased BigQuery + Metabase consolidation and Looker sunset plan
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice@bluehaven-analytics.com>, David Wu <david.wu@google.com>, Samira Khan <samira@metabase.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: phased BigQuery + Metabase consolidation and Looker sunset plan

Hi Alice / David / Samira —

Thanks for the renewal heads-up, Alice. Bluehaven's current contract runs through Q3 and you've flagged wanting clearer unit economics before renewing. We've run a quick internal evaluation and think there's an opportunity to reduce your stack complexity and lower run-rate by consolidating reporting onto BigQuery + Metabase, with a phased deprecation of Looker over 9–12 months.

Attached is our first-pass cost model (bq_cost_model_v2.xlsx) and a very high-level migration playbook. Key framing:
- Phase 1 (0–3 months): move reporting endpoints and high-volume dashboards to BigQuery materialized views, keep Looker read-only for legacy dashboards.
- Phase 2 (3–6 months): implement Metabase for operational dashboards, migrate ~60% of Looker content.
- Phase 3 (6–12 months): complete migration, turn off legacy Looker models; post-termination support window of 30 days.

Benefits we estimate for Bluehaven: 18–27% lower monthly spend (BigQuery committed usage + Metabase operational costs vs current Looker + BI engine), faster query TTF for common dashboards, and lower touch for analytics platform engineering. Numbers in the sheet are preliminary — Marcus and I will refine if this direction makes sense.

As next steps: can you confirm the primary constraints (contractual terms with Looker, any data residency needs, and preferred go-live window)? David — any notes on committed-use discounts that would materially change the model assumptions? Samira — can Metabase offer a migration SOW + timeline and note any SI partners you recommend?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: bq_cost_model_v2.xlsx, migration_playbook_draft.md
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Alice Monroe <alice@bluehaven-analytics.com>, David Wu <david.wu@google.com>, Samira Khan <samira@metabase.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased BigQuery + Metabase consolidation and Looker sunset plan

Neha — quick read, looks good. A couple of notes from the cost side:
- The sheet assumes a 3-year BigQuery commit for 30% of current peak usage. If Bluehaven wants a 1-year commit we'll need to show the delta; I can add a 12-month vs 36-month tab.
- We should call out egress assumptions: cross-region joins and BI engine cache behavior add non-trivial costs. Put a conservative egress line item in the model.

Operational questions for the client: do they rely on LookML for governance that Metabase needs to replicate? If yes, migration effort grows to ~1.2–1.5x.

I'll follow up with a refined cost workbook by Friday (2026-05-28).

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Hi Neha / Alice / Marcus —

Thanks for the summary. Metabase can support a phased migration and we have a standard migration SOW that covers schema mapping, dashboard rebuild, and QA. High-level pricing (ballpark):
- Migration SOW: $35k–$70k depending on LookML complexity and number of dashboards (we'll need a list).
- Subscription: $8k–$15k/month for our hosted offering at the scale you described (RB <-> 200M rows / month).
- Optional: Partner-managed migration for an additional fee; we can introduce partners who have done Looker -> Metabase conversions.

We can provide the SOW draft and reference customers if that helps procurement. Also — we'll cover the first 20 hours of migration planning at no charge to help scope.

Team —

Legal/procurement here. A few procurement items to lock down before we send a commercial recommendation to Bluehaven:
1) SOW clarity — we need a firm statement of work with milestones, acceptance criteria, and an IP/data handling clause (attachable to the main contract). Samira, please send the SOW draft to lauren.bishop@redwood.com and cc legal_ops@redwood.com.
2) Transition support — request that Metabase include a 30-day runbook and 60-day hypercare in the SOW (we shouldn't be on the hook for extended support).
3) Discount ladder — for a 12-month commitment to Metabase subscription + a 3-year BigQuery commit, propose a blended discount: 12% off Metabase subscription and an additional $15k migration credit. Ask partners for written confirmation.
4) Data residency — Bluehaven has a EU data subset; ensure BigQuery regions and Metabase hosting options can meet that. David, can you confirm region-level options and latency expectations for EU parcels?

If we can get SOW + pricing commitments this week, I will redline and circulate a single-deal recommendation.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
